rows.source: Terry Branstad, onye nnọchite anya U.S na China bụkwa onye chịburu Iowa, onye mbupu ahịa nri ubi nke ukwuu na China, kwuru na China merụrụ ndị ọrụ, ndị ọrụ ugbo na azụmahịa nke America ahụ.
rows.output: Terry Branstad, the U.S. Trade Representative to China and former governor of Iowa, which is a major agricultural exporter to China, said that China has harmed American workers, farmers, and businesses.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: China, Branstad dere n’echiche ya na Des Moines Register na Sọnde, “na-ekwusi ike maka mmegide ahụ site na itinye mgbasa ozi n’akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi anyị.”
rows.output: China, Branstad wrote in his column in the Des Moines Register on Sunday, "emphasized the opposition by placing ads in our newspapers."
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: “N’ịgbasa ozi asị a, gọọmentị China na ewere oghere omenala America hụrụ n’anya bụ nke onye kwuo uche ya na mgbasa ozi enweghị mkpagbu were tinye mgbasa ozi akwụrụ ụgwọ na Des Moines Register.” Branstad dere.
rows.output: "In spreading this false information, the Chinese government has taken advantage of the cherished freedom of the press in America, which is protected by our First Amendment, and has inserted paid advertising in the Des Moines Register." Branstad wrote.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: “Ma ịtụlee ya n’ọdụ akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi dị n’okporo beijing ebe a, ịga ahụ na enwere obere olu ndịiche nke na ịghaghị ahụ ihe n’egosi n’ezie echiche di iche ndị China nwere ike nwee maka usoro akụnụba China nọ na nsogbu, ebe ọ bụ n’ụlọ mgbasa ozi nọ na njikwa nke China Communist Party,” ọ dere.
rows.output: "But when you look at the media outlets in Beijing, you can see that there are only a few voices that are different from the official line, and you have to look very hard to find any real dissenting views that the Chinese people might have about the Chinese economic system, which is in trouble, because the media is controlled by the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na “otu n’ime akwụkwọ akụkọ ama ama na China zenarịrị ibiputa” ederede ya, n’agbanyeghị na o kwughị akwụkwọ akụkọ nke ọ bụ.
rows.output: He also added that "one of the most popular Chinese novels that has been avoided from being published" was his writing, although he did not mention the novel.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ndị Repọblikan Na-akpachapụ Ndị Ntuli Aka Ụmụ-nwanyị Tupu Ntuli Aka Ọkara Ọchịchị Maka Ọgbaghara Kavanaugh, Ndị Nyocha Dọrọ Aka na Ntị
rows.output: The Republican Party is trying to suppress the votes of women before the midterm elections due to the confirmation of Kavanaugh, the Supreme Court Justice.
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Dị ka ọtụtụ ndị isi Repọblikan kwụnyere ma kwuchitere Onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu Brett Kavanaugh n’ihu ebubo dị iche iche nke mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị, ndị nyocha adọọla aka na ntị na ha ga-ahụ ndapụta iwe ga-esite ọkachasị n’aka ụmụ-nwanyị, n’oge ntuli aka ọkara ọchịchị na-abịa.
rows.output: Like many Republican leaders who endorsed and defended Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of numerous allegations of sexual misconduct, investigators have warned that they will be looking for signs of increased anger particularly from women, in the upcoming midterm elections.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Mmetụta sochiri nke a dị elu nke ukwuu, na ọtụtụ ndị Repọblikan ka edekọbara na ha egosila na ha chọrọ ịga n’ihu mee ntuli aka.
rows.output: The consequences of this were so severe that many Republicans were recorded as saying that they wanted to continue the election.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Enweghị ike iweghachi ihe ndị ahụ,” Grant Reeher, onye ọkammụta nke sayensị ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na Syracuse University Maxwell School gwara The Hill maka ederede nke ebiputara na Satọde.
rows.output: They can't be recovered," Grant Reeher, a political science professor at Syracuse University's Maxwell School, told The Hill in a Saturday post.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reeher kwuru na ya na-agbagha n’ọkwụkwa ikpeazụ nke Onye Ọmebe Iwu Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) mere maka nyocha FBI a ga-ezu iji wetuo iwe ndị ntuli aka.
rows.output: Reeher said he was disappointed in the last-minute amendment by Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) that would delay the FBI's investigation to address the concerns of voters.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: “Ụmụ-nwanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụnyahụ - ha agaghị echefu echi niile ma Nọvemba, “ Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ senịọ na onye nkwuchite okwu obodo maka otu ọganihu MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dabere na akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday - they will not forget tomorrow and November, " Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, said on Friday, according to the Washington Post.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: N’ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị ngagharị iwe kwere ukwe “Nọvemba na-abịa!” ka ha na-agagharị ngagharị iwe n’ogologo ụzọ Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu ebe ndị Repọblikan ji Ọgbakọ Ọka Ikpe họrọ ịga n’ihu na nhọrọ Kavanaugh agbanyeghị nkwuputa Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kwuputara.
rows.output: On Friday morning, protesters chanted "November is coming!" as they marched through the streets of the Capitol Hill neighborhood where Republicans decided to proceed with the confirmation of Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: “Ịnụ ọkụ n’obi na mkpalite mmụọ nke Demokrat ga-apụ iche,” Stu Rothenberg, onye nyocha ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị enweghị otu o binyere gwara ndị akụkọ.
rows.output: "The enthusiasm and the inspiration of the Democrats will be different," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told reporters.
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: “Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke a bụ eziokwu.
rows.output: "People say that it's high; this is true.
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Mana ọ nwere ike ịgbagokwu ọkachasị n’etiti ụmụ-nwanyị n’enweghị otu ha binyere n’ime obodo yana ndị ntuli aka na-etolite etolite, gbara afọ 18- ruo 29-, bụ ndị ebe onye isi ala anaghị amasị, anaghị eme ntuli aka kwa mgbe.”
rows.output: But it can be most pronounced among women without a partner in the countryside and among young voters, aged 18 to 29, who are in areas where the president is not liked, and who do not vote regularly.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Ọbụlagodi tupu nkwuputanke ọha Ford mere na-akọwa ebubo mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị megide onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe kachasị Elu, ndị nyocha na-atụ elo na ndapụta iwe nwere ike sote ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Repọblikan gaa n’ihu mee nkwado ahụ.
rows.output: Even before Ford's public statement, the investigators were already anticipating a potential backlash if the Republicans were to proceed with the endorsement.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Nke a abụrụla ọgbaghara dịịrị GOP,” Michael Steele kwuru, onye isi chịburu Ọgbakọ Otu Repọblikan, na mbido izug ara aga, dabere na NBC News.
rows.output: "This has been a disaster for the GOP," said Michael Steele, the former chairman of the Republican National Committee, on the eve of the election, as reported by NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.
rows.output: "It's not just about the primaries or the final election or whether Kavanaugh was confirmed, but also about how the Republicans managed this issue and how they treated it," Guy Cecil, the president of Priorities USA, a Democratic group, told reporters.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.output: In fact, Americans are as divided as they were on whom to trust Ford and Kavanaugh, with more than half siding with the latter.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.
rows.output: A new survey from YouGov shows that 41% of respondents completely agree or somewhat agree with Ford's statements, while 35% completely agree or somewhat agree with Kavanaugh's statements.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.
rows.output: Furthermore, 38 percent said they believed that Kavanaugh was probably lying or definitely lying during his testimony, while only 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.
rows.output: After Flake's nomination, the FBI is now investigating Ford's allegations, as well as at least one other allegation, made by Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.
rows.output: Ford made a statement in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee last week that Kavanaugh assaulted her when she was 17 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez was accused by the Supreme Court nominee of showing off his wealth during social gatherings during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook
rows.output: The World Wide Web inventor is planning to launch a new Internet to compete with Google and Facebook
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is starting a new company that will compete with Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.output: The new tech-savvy plan, Inrupt, is a startup that is building on Berners-Lee's open-source software, Solid.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.
rows.output: Solid provides users with the flexibility to choose where they want to store their data and information that people can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”
rows.output: In a special interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee quipped that the purpose of Inrupt was "to rule the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
rows.output: "We will do it now," he said for the new house.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”
rows.output: "It is time to register for the history."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid enye ndị mmadụ oghere imepụta “ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị” ma ọ bụ POD.
rows.output: The device uses Solid technology to provide individuals with a "personal online data vault" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: It can have a contact list, a to-do list, a calendar, a music library, and personal and work apps.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n’otu nchọgharị ma ha niile n’otu oge.
rows.output: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify all in one browser and all at once.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.
rows.output: The unique feature of a personal online database is that it is only accessible to the person who created it, and they decide who gets to see any information.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”
rows.output: The company calls it "personalization by data."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.
rows.output: Inrupt's mission, based on CEO John Bruce, is to bring together companies, resources, systems, and expertise to help Solid reach everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.
rows.output: The company had only Berners-Lee, Bruce, IBM's storage division, and a team of engineers hired to work on the project, as well as a group of volunteer coders.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.
rows.output: By the end of this year, global tech manufacturers will be able to create their own non-invasive devices using Inrupt's hardware and software.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that his team was not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether they would start or abandon the radical change where the business model is turned upside down with the user's gaze.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”
rows.output: "We do not accept them."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”
rows.output: In a Medium post on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that the goal of Inrupt is to empower businesses and the environment by providing a new web platform built on Solid.
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee revolutionized the Internet by creating the World Wide Web Consortium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.
rows.output: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal advocate for the freedom of the internet.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Ọbulagodi mgbe a na-ebuputa Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọrọ dịka onye Mmepụta na Onye Isi nke World Wide Web Consortuim, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.
rows.output: Berners-Lee will continue to serve as the inventor and chair of the World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation, and the Open Data Institute during the launch of Inrupt.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: “A na m enwe olile anya nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa n’ihu nke weebu,” Berners-Lee gbakwunyere.
rows.output: "We are very optimistic about the future of the web," Berners-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: Emere emume onye ụkọchukwu Victoria Cross WW1
rows.output: Bernard Vann: A ceremony for the WW1 Victoria Cross priest
rows.reference: Bernard Vann: WW1 Victoria Cross cleric celebrated

rows.source: Emeela emume nke naanị ụkọchukwu Church of England nwetara mmeri Victoria Cross n’oge World War One dị ka onye agha n’obodo ya ka afọ gbara 100.
rows.output: A ceremony was held for the only Church of England priest to win the Victoria Cross in World War One, as a soldier in his home town, 100 years after his death.
rows.reference: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.

rows.source: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann nwetara awọdụ na 29, Septemba 1918 na mbuso agha emere na Bellenglise na Lehaucourt.
rows.output: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann was awarded the Distinguished Service Order on 29 September 1918 for the attack on Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.
rows.reference: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, mgbọ ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe tụrụ ya ka ụbọchị anọ gachara na ọ maghị ncha ncha na etubere ya ugo ndị agha kachasị na Britain.
rows.output: However, a bullet wound to the chest four days later left him unaware of the decorations and honors bestowed upon him by the British Army.
rows.reference: However, he was killed by a sniper four days later and never knew he had won the highest British military honour.

rows.source: Ụmụ ụmụ ya ndị nwoke abụọ kpughere okwute iji na-eme ncheta ya na ngarube emere na Rushden, Northamptonshire, na Satọde.
rows.output: His two sons unveiled a stone to commemorate him at a service held in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.
rows.reference: A commemorative stone was unveiled by his two grandsons at a parade in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.

rows.output: The German Navy's new Frigate is expected to be commissioned in 2014 to replace the Cold War-era frigates that are now obsolete, but it will not be deployed until at least next year due to technical problems and high costs, the national press reported.
rows.reference: German Navy's newest frigate should have been commissioned in 2014 to replace ageing Cold War-era warships, but it won't be there until at least the next year due to faulty systems and snowballing cost, local media reported.

rows.output: The deployment of the "Rheinland-Pfalz," the lead ship of the new Baden-Wuerttemberg-class frigate, has been delayed until mid-2019, according to the newspaper Die Zeit, citing a defense official.
rows.reference: Commissioning of the "Rheinland-Pfalz," the lead ship of the brand new Baden-Wuerttemberg-class frigates, has now been postponed until the first half of 2019, according to Die Zeit newspaper citing a military spokesman.

rows.reference: The vessel should have joined the Navy in 2014, but the troubling post-delivery issues plagued the fate of the ambitious project.

rows.source: Ụgbọ Baden-Wuerttemberg-class anọ Ndị Agha Mmiri tụrụ ahịa ya na 2007 ga-abịa dịka nnọchi anya Bremen-class frigate kabagoro nka.
rows.output: The four Baden-Wuerttemberg-class corvettes of the German Navy were sold in 2007 and will come as a replacement for the Bremen-class frigate.
rows.reference: The four Baden-Wuerttemberg-class vessels the Navy ordered back in 2007 will come as replacement to the ageing Bremen-class frigates.

rows.output: Other important tasks, including the time required for its construction, have been a factor - it should be noted that it would be possible to deploy the new frigates in a period of up to two years from the shipyard.

rows.source: Frigate F125 ahụ juputara na nsogbu pụtara n’isi akụkọ n’afọ gara aga mgbe Ndị Agha Mmiri nke Germany jụrụ itinye ụgbọ ahụ n’ọrụ wee bughachi ya na ọdụ nrụpụta ụgbọ mmiri Blohm & Voss dị na Hamburg.
rows.output: The F125 frigate was full of problems that emerged at the beginning of the year when the German Navy refused to put the ship into service and sent it back to the Blohm & Voss shipyard in Hamburg for repairs.
rows.reference: The ill-fated F125 frigate made headlines last year, when the German Navy officially refused to commission the vessel and returned it to Blohm & Voss shipyard in Hamburg.

rows.source: Ntakịrị ka amatara maka ihe kpatara eji bughachi ya, mana ndị ụlọ mgbasa ozi Germany rụtụrụ aka ọnụọgụ ihe ole ma ole “mmebi ngwanro na ngwaike “ dị oke mkpa, nke mere na ngwa ọgụ ahụ abaghị uru ma ọ bụrụ na-ebupu ya ka ọ gaa agha.
rows.output: A little was known about the reasons for its return, but German media pointed out the number of "computer and electronic equipment" that was deemed too sensitive, making the weapon useless if it was to be sent to the front.

rows.output: The software is not sufficient as it is, as 120 sailors will be needed to operate the Baden-Wuerttemberg-class ship - only half the number of sailors needed to operate the Bremen-class frigate.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na ọ bụ ihe “na-atụ uche” na Toyota UK gwara BBC na ọ bụrụ na Britain apụọ na EU na-enweghị nkwekọrịta, na ha ga-akwụsị nwa oge ịrụpụta ihe n’ụlọ nrụpụta dị na Burnaston, n’akụkụ Derby.
rows.output: He added that it was "unfortunate" that Toyota UK told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal, they would have to temporarily stop production at their plant in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: “Anyị chọrọ nkwekọrịta,” Mr Clark kwuru.
rows.output: "We need a deal," Mr. Clark said.

rows.source: Onye ọrụ ụgbọ ala nke Japan ahụ kwuru na ndapụta nke igbu oge n’oke ala ma ọ bụrụ na enweghị nkwekọrịta Brexit nwere ike napụ ọrụ.

rows.output: The Burnaston plant, which manufactures the Toyota Auris and Avensis, produced around 150,000 vehicles last year, with 90% of them exported to other European Union countries.
rows.reference: The Burnaston plant - which makes Toyota's Auris and Avensis - produced nearly 150,000 cars last year of which 90% were exported to the rest of the European Union.

rows.source: “Echiche m bụ na ọ bụrụ na Britain apụọ na EU na ngwucha Maachị, anyị ga-ahụ na nrụpụta kwụsịrị n’ụlọ nrụpụta anyị” Marvin Cooke onye isi njikwa Toyota na Burnaston kwuru.

rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on March 29, there could be a shortage of parts that car manufacturers say could lead to delays and incomplete vehicles.

rows.source: Ekpebiri na pasentị 13 bụ ndị na abụghị ndị bi na UK na azụta akụ ndị London arụrụ ọhụrụ, na ebugo ụgwọ ma na eme ka o sie ike maka ndị na eme nzụta izizi ha iji nweta ọganihu n’nzọụkwụ obibi ụlọ.

rows.reference: He accused big construction firms of keeping property prices high by snapping up land but not using it, and urged Mrs May to abandon quotas on affordable homes to fix Britain's "housing disgrace."

rows.source: Jack Ross: ‘Ọchịchọ m kachasị bụ ijikwa Scotland’
rows.output: Jack Ross: 'My greatest wish is to manage Scotland'

rows.source: Onye isi nke Sunderland Jack Ross kwuru na “ọchịchọ ya kachasị” bụ ịbụrụ onye ndu Scotland otu oge.
rows.output: Sunderland's head coach Jack Ross said his "biggest wish" is to be Scotland's manager one day.
rows.reference: Sunderland boss Jack Ross says his "ultimate ambition" is to become the Scotland manager at some stage.

rows.source: Onye Scotland ahụ, 42, na enwe obi ụtọ maka mgba nke iweghachite otu asọmpi North-East, ndị nọ ugbu a n’ọkwa atọ na League One, akara atọ n’okpuru nke isi.
rows.output: The 42-year-old Scot is delighted with the challenge of trying to win the North-East title, with the current third-placed team in League One, three points clear of the top.
rows.reference: The Scot, 42, is relishing the challenge of reviving the North-East club, who currently sit third place in League One, three points off the top.

rows.source: Ọ gara na Stadium of Light n’ọkọchị a ka o duchara St Mirren laghachite na Scottish Premiership n’afọ asọmpi gara aga.
rows.output: He went to the Stadium of Light in the summer to watch St Mirren return to the Scottish Premiership in the previous season's campaign.
rows.reference: He moved to the Stadium of Light this summer after guiding St Mirren back to the Scottish Premiership last season.

rows.source: “Achọburu m ịgbara obodo m bọọlụ ka m bụ onye egwu.
rows.output: I wanted to kick my country in the balls as I was a football player.
rows.reference: "I wanted to play for my country as a player.

rows.source: Enwetara m cap B nke ahụ bụ ya,” Ross gwara Sportsound nke BBC Scotland.
rows.output: I got that B cap, that was it," Ross told BBC Scotland's Sportsound.
rows.reference: I got a B cap and that was it," Ross told BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

rows.source: “Mana etolitere m na elele Scotland na Hampden ọtụtụ oge, mụ na nna m ka m bụ nwata, ọ bụ ihe na adọghachi m oge niile.
rows.output: But I grew up watching Scotland at Hampden many times, me and my dad when I was a kid, it's something that always draws me back.
rows.reference: "But I grew up watching Scotland at Hampden a lot with my dad as a kid, and it is always something that has drawn me back.

rows.source: Ohere ahụ ga-abịa, agbanyeghị, ọ bụrụ na m mee nke ọma na njikwa otu egwuregwu.”
rows.output: The opportunity will come, however, if I do well in managing the team's game.
rows.reference: That opportunity would only come, though, if I am successful in club management."

rows.output: Those who came before Ross as Sunderland's leader included Dick Advocaat, David Moyes, Sam Allardyce, Martin O'Neill, Roy Keane, Gue Poyet, and Paulo Di Canio.
rows.reference: Ross's predecessors as Sunderland manager include Dick Advocaat, David Moyes, Sam Allardyce, Martin O'Neill, Roy Keane, Gus Poyet and Paulo Di Canio.

rows.source: Onye isi nke Alloa Athletic gara aga kwuru na ọ naghị enwe ụjọ n’isochi aha ndị ahụ ama ama n’ụdịrị nnukwu otu ahụ, ka ọ jụchara arịrịọ ndị si na Barnsley na Ipswich Town.
rows.output: The former manager of Alloa Athletic said he was not afraid to follow in the footsteps of those famous names in the great tradition of the club, after rejecting approaches from Barnsley and Ipswich Town.
rows.reference: The former Alloa Athletic boss says he felt no trepidation in following such established names at such a big club, having previously rejected overtures from Barnsley and Ipswich Town.

rows.source: “Ọganihu maka m n’oge a ka a ga-atụ site na “enwere m ike idughachi otu a na Premier League?’
rows.output: "Progress for me in this period is measured by 'Can I bring this team back to the Premier League?'"
rows.reference: "Success for me at the moment will be gauged by 'can I return this club to the Premier League?'

rows.source: N’ihi nyiwe na ụlọ nke otu a, na enweghị mgbagha kwesịrị ịnọ na Premier League,” o kwuru.

rows.output: "It's not an easy task to return there, but I can only see myself as a person who succeeded here if I can bring that same mentality back there."
rows.reference: "It is not an easy task to get it there, but I would probably only view myself as being successful here if I can get the club back there."

rows.source: “Ekwenyere n’ezie na njikwa bụ ihe ziri m nke ọma, karịa ịgba agba.

rows.source: Mana ịgba agba na esi ike.

rows.output: There are many things you have to go through every week.

rows.output: I was able to go through that in the context of the problem and the rigidity of the work, but the management was good in terms of the view.
rows.reference: I still go through that in terms of the stresses and pressure of the job but management just feels right.

rows.source: Bido na mbụ achọrọ m ịme njikwa, ugbu a ana m eme ya, ọ kachasị enye m mmetụta obi ume ala, abụ m onwe m na ndụ okenye m niile.”
rows.output: First, I wanted to be in control, now I am, it's the most empowering feeling, I am myself in my adult life."

rows.output: The summer heat has caused a drop in sales for British pubs but has created more problems for the restaurant business.
rows.reference: The summer heatwave has boosted takings for Britain's struggling pubs but heaped more pressure on restaurant chains.

rows.source: Otu ndị ụlọ mmanya hụrụ ka ahịa rịgoro pasentị 2.7 na Julaị - mana nrite n’ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ dara pasentị 4.8, ọnụọgụ gosiri.
rows.output: The Hotel Association saw sales rise by 2.7% in July - but restaurant profits fell by 4.8%, the figures showed.
rows.reference: Pub and bar groups saw sales rise 2.7 per cent in July - but takings in restaurants were down 4.8 per cent, figures revealed.

rows.source: Peter Martin, nke ndị ndụmọdụ azụmahịa CGA, nke kpokọrọ ọnụọgụ ahụ, kwuru: “Anyanwụ ka dị yana nsonye England na World Cup toro ogologo ole atụrụ anya pụtara na Julaị sochiri otu usoro ka ọnwa nke Juun gara aga, mgbe ụlọ mmanya rịgoro pasentị 2.8, belụsọ na ndị ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ nwere nnukwu nhịahụ.
rows.output: Peter Martin, from CGA's Advisory Board, which compiled the numbers, said: "The sun is still shining and England's World Cup participation has boosted sales in July by as much as they were in June, when bars rose by 2.8 percent, except for restaurants, which had a poor month."
rows.reference: Peter Martin, of business consultancy CGA, which compiled the figures, said: "Continued sunshine and England's longer than expected participation in the World Cup meant July followed a similar pattern to the previous month of June, when pubs were up 2.8 per cent, except that restaurants were hit even harder.

rows.source: Nrịda nke pasentị 1.8 n’azụmahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ na Juun kawanyere njọ na Julai.
rows.output: A decrease of 1.8 percent in the restaurant business in June was worse in July.
rows.reference: The fall of 1.8 per cent in restaurant trading in June just got worse in July.

rows.source: Ụlọ mmanya kachasị mee nke ọma otu yitere ihe dị ka otu ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ si gbadaa.
rows.output: The best bar in the world is like a restaurant falling down.
rows.reference: Drink-led pubs and bars performed by far the strongest with like-for-likes up more than restaurants were down.

rows.source: Ụlọ mmanya na ere nri tara ahụhụ n’anyanwụ, mana ọbụghị ka nke ndị na azụ ahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ.

rows.output: He said, "I don't want any parent to feel the kind of pain I feel every day."

rows.output: Ms. Davis, 45, from Lydney, said her son is a talented chef and has a promising future with a smile and a spring in his step.

rows.output: They always say that his laughter and the lifting of every room are the best things about him.

rows.output: However, he stopped working before he died, because he was "in a very bad state."
rows.reference: However, he gave up work before he died, as he was "in a really dark place."

rows.output: Ms. Davis said: "I've always thought that we would eventually feel the effects of climate change."
rows.reference: Ms Davis said: "I continually worry that there's going to be a knock on effect."

rows.output: The silence was deafening - you should have said something.

rows.output: Ms. Humphreys, who had been friends with Ms. Davies for many years, was not close to Mark, her husband of 15 years, in the short time after his mother's death.

rows.output: He was in a dream on Christmas morning - when my children opened their gifts to him and those they had not wrapped or anything.

rows.output: Brett Kavanaugh's future hangs in the balance as the FBI begins an investigation

rows.output: I think if we can get something like what it's asking for - a review of the restrictions in real time, a review of the scope of the restrictions - we might be able to get some small degree of unity," Mr. Flake said on Saturday, adding that he was concerned that the conference was "overly" in the grip of the political restrictions.
rows.reference: "I thought, if we could actually get something like what he was asking for - an investigation limited in time, limited in scope - we could maybe bring a little unity," said Mr Flake on Saturday, adding that he feared the committee was "falling apart" amid entrenched partisan gridlock.

rows.source: Gịnị kpatara na Maazị Kavanaugh na ndị nkwado Repọblikan achọghị ka ndị FBI mee nyocha?
rows.output: Why do Mr. Kavanaugh and Republican supporters not want the FBI to investigate?

rows.output: I have no interest in it because of the time.

rows.reference: The midterm elections are only five weeks away, on November 6 - if, as expected, the Republicans do badly, then they will be severely weakened in their attempts to get the man they want elected to the highest court in the land.

rows.source: George W. Bush na ewelite ekwentị iji kpọọ Ndị Ọmeiwu, na arịọ ha ka ha kwado Maazị Kavanaugh, onye rụrụ ọrụ na White House n’aka Maazị Bush ma site n’aka ya zute nwunye ya Ashley, onye nke bụ ọde akwụkwọ nkeonwe Maazị Bush.
rows.output: George W. Bush pulled out his phone to call the Senators, asking them to support Mr. Kavanaugh, who worked in the White House for Mr. Bush and met his wife Ashley, who was Mr. Bush's personal secretary.

rows.output: He will not look away from Mr. Kavanaugh, and he will not be swayed by the fact that he may receive at least 50 votes in the Senate, which would allow Vice President Mike Pence to break the tie and confirm him to the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: It's still not clear whether Mr Kavanaugh can get to at least 50 votes on the Senate floor, which would allow Mike Pence, the vice president, to break a tie and confirm him to the Supreme Court.

rows.source: Ọnụọgụ ndị gbapụrụ na North Korea ‘gbadara’ n’okpuru Kim
rows.output: The number of defectors from North Korea 'fell' under Kim.
rows.reference: North Korea defector numbers 'drop' under Kim

rows.source: Ọnụọgụ ndị gbapụrụ na North Korea gbagara South Korea agbadaala kemgbe Kim Jong-un banyere n’ọchịchị afọ asaa gara aga, onye ọmebe iwu South Korea kwuru.
rows.output: The number of defectors from North Korea who fled to South Korea has decreased since Kim Jong-un took power seven years ago, a South Korean lawmaker said.
rows.reference: The number of North Korean defectors to South Korea has fallen since Kim Jong-un came to power seven years ago, a South Korean lawmaker has said.

rows.source: Park Byeong-seun, na arụtụ aka na data si na minitri njikọta South, kwuru na enweela mgbapụ 1,127 n’afọ gara aga - tụlee yana 2,706 na 2011.
rows.output: Park Byeong-seun, citing data from the South Korean Ministry of Unification, stated that there were 1,127 cases of defection in the previous year - compare with 2,706 in 2011.
rows.reference: Park Byeong-seug, citing data from the South's unification ministry, said there had been 1,127 defections last year - compared with 2,706 in 2011.

rows.source: Maazị Park kwuru njikwa oke ala kpachikwuru akpachi n’etiti North Korea na China yana ụgwọ dị elu ndị na akpọfe ndị mmadụ na ana socha n’ihe ndị kpatara ya.
rows.output: Mr. Park said that the management of the North Korea-China border is a high-cost, high-risk endeavor that is not sustainable.
rows.reference: Mr Park said tighter border controls between North Korea and China and higher rates charged by people smugglers were key factors.

rows.source: Pyongyang agwabeghị ọhaneze ihe ọ bụla.
rows.output: Pyongyang has not yet made any public statement.
rows.reference: Pyongyang has made no public comments.

rows.source: A na enye ọtụtụ nke ndị gbapụrụ si na North akwụkwọ amaala nke South Korea.
rows.output: We provide many of the refugees from the North with the National Identity Number of South Korea.
rows.reference: The vast majority of defectors from the North are eventually offered South Korean citizenship.

rows.source: Seoul kwuru na ihe gafere ndị North Korea 30,000 gafere oke ala ahụ n’ụzọ dara iwu kemgbe ngwụcha nke Ọgụ Korea na 1953.
rows.output: Seoul said that more than 30,000 North Koreans have crossed the border illegally since the end of the Korean War in 1953.
rows.reference: Seoul says more than 30,000 North Koreans have illegally crossed the border since the end of the Korean War in 1953.

rows.source: Imirikiti na esi China agbapụ, nke nwere oke ala kachasị ogologo n’etiti North Korea ma ka dị mfe ịgafe karịa Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) echedosiri ike n’etiti Korea abụọ ahụ.
rows.output: The Chinese border, which has the longest land border between North Korea and South Korea, is easier to cross than the heavily fortified Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) between the two Koreas.
rows.reference: Most flee via China, which has the longest border with North Korea and is easier to cross than the heavily protected Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) between the two Koreas.

rows.output: China has seen a surge in illegal crossings, with more people crossing the border on foot than on foot, and a rise in the number of people being sent back due to anger.
rows.reference: China regards the defectors as illegal migrants rather than refugees and often forcibly repatriates them.

rows.source: Mmekọrịta n’etiti North na South - ndị ka nọ n’ọgụ - enwela mmelite ahụrụ anya n’ọnwa nso nso a.
rows.output: The relationship between the North and South - the two sides still in conflict - has seen a noticeable improvement in recent months.
rows.reference: Relations between the North and the South - who are still technically at war - have markedly improved in recent months.

rows.source: Na mbido ọnwa a, ndị isi nke obodo abụọ ahụ hụrụ na Pyongyang maka ekwumekwu gbadoro na ụbụbọ mkposa ngwa ọgụ nuklịa.
rows.output: At the beginning of the month, the leaders of the two countries visited Pyongyang for talks focused on the dismantling of nuclear weapons.
rows.reference: Earlier this month, the leaders of the two countries met in Pyongyang for talks that centred on the stalled denuclearisation negotiations.

rows.source: Nke a bịara ka nnukwu nzụkọ Juun mere n’etiti Onye Isi Ala Donald Trump na Kim Jong-un na Singapore, mgbe ha kwenyere n’isiokwu sara mbara iji rụkọta ọrụ maka ala mmiri Korea na enweghị ngwa ọgụ nuklịa.
rows.output: This came after a major summit in June between President of the United States Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un in Singapore, where they agreed on a broad range of issues to work together for Korean Peninsula peace and denuclearization.
rows.reference: This came after June's historic meeting between US President Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un in Singapore, when they agreed in broad terms to work towards the nuclear-free Korean peninsula.

rows.source: Mana na Satọde, Minista Ofesi nke North Korea Ri Yong-ho tara ntaramahụhụ ndị US ụta maka ọganihu na adịghị kemgbe ahụ.
rows.output: On Saturday, North Korean Foreign Minister Ri Yong-ho accused the US of being responsible for the lack of progress in the talks.
rows.reference: But on Saturday, North Korean Foreign Minister Ri Yong-ho blamed US sanctions for the lack of progress since then.

rows.source: “Na enweghị ntụkwasị obi na US, agaghị enwe okwukwe na nchedo obodo anyị yana n’ụdịrị ọnọdụ ndị ahụ, enweghị ụzọ ọ bụla anyị ga-esi bụrụ ụzọ kwekọrịta otu oge ịkwasa ngwa ọgụ anyị,” Maazị Ri kwuru n’okwu na Mgbakọ Ezumezu UN na New York.
rows.output: “Lacking confidence in the US, we will not have faith in the protection of our country and in the kind of circumstances that exist, there is no way we can be a compatible path to spread our weapons,” Mr. Ri said in a speech at the UN General Assembly in New York.
rows.reference: "Without any trust in the US, there will be no confidence in our national security and under such circumstances, there is no way we will unilaterally disarm ourselves first," Mr Ri said in a speech to the UN General Assembly in New York.

rows.source: Nancy Pelosi kpọrọ Brett Kavanaugh “isi mgbaka,” o kwuru na o tozughi iji rụọ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị
rows.output: Nancy Pelosi called Brett Kavanaugh "a coward," saying he was not worthy of serving on the Supreme Court.
rows.reference: Nancy Pelosi calls Brett Kavanaugh "hysterical," says he is unfit to serve on the Supreme Court

rows.source: Onye Ndu Ndị Ntakịrị N’ụlọ Nzụkọ Nancy Pelosi kpọrọ onye nhọpụta maka Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Kavanaugh “isi mgbaka” ma kwuo na ọ na ewe iwe ọkụ iji rụọ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị.
rows.output: Nancy Pelosi, onye ndu ndị nta n'ụlọ nzukọ, kpọrọ onye nhọpụta maka Ụlọ Ikpe Kasị Elu nke Kavanaugh "isi mgbaka" ma kwuo na ọ na ewe iwe ọkụ iji rụọ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kasị Elu.
rows.reference: House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi called Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh "hysterical" and said that he was temperamentally unfit to serve on the Supreme Court.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru okwu ndị ahụ n’ajụjụ ọnụ na Satọde na Texas Tribune Festival na Austin, Texas.
rows.output: Pelosi made those remarks in an interview on Saturday at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin, Texas.
rows.reference: Pelosi made the comments in an interview Saturday at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin, Texas.

rows.source: “Enwenwughi m ike ịkwụsị ịche na ọ bụrụ na nwanyị mee ụdịrị ihe ahụ, ha ga-ekwu ‘isi mgbaka,”” Pelosi kwuru maka mmetụta ya n’ihe akaebe Kavanaugh n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe nke Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu na Tọsde.
rows.output: "I can't help but think that if a woman had done the same thing, they would have said 'head slap,'" said Pelosi, referring to the impact of Kavanaugh's testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Thursday.
rows.reference: "I couldn't help but think that if a woman had ever performed that way, they would say 'hysterical,'" Pelosi said about her reaction to Kavanaugh's testimony before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Thursday.

rows.source: Kavanaugh jiri nnukwu mwute gọnarị ebubo ndị ahụ na ọ wakporo Dk. Christine Blasey Ford n’ike mgbe ha abụọ bụ ndị ntorobịa.
rows.output: Kavanaugh denied the allegations of sexual assault against Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, claiming that he was a victim of a false accusation.
rows.reference: Kavanaugh emotionally denied allegations that he had sexually assaulted Dr. Christine Blasey Ford when they were both teenagers.

rows.source: N’oge nkwupute mmepe ya, mmụọ Kavanaugh di elu nke ukwuu, oge ụfọdụ ọ na achọ iti mkpu ma olu a na agbagbu ya ka ọ na ekwu maka ezinụlọ ya yana afọ ụlọ akwụkwọ kọleji ya.
rows.output: During his confirmation hearing, Kavanaugh's spirit was so high that at times he wanted to shout, but his voice was choked with emotion as he spoke about his family and his college years.
rows.reference: During his opening statement, Kavanaugh was very emotional, at times nearly shouting and choking up while discussing his family and his high school years.

rows.source: Ọ kọtọkwara ndị Demokrat nọ n’ọgbakọ ahụ n’ụzọ doro anya, na akpọ ebubo emere ya “mgbagbu omume dị egwu n’anya, akpara akpa” nke ndị mmesapụ ahụ na ewe iwe na Hillary Clinton dara na ntuli aka onye isi ala 2016 haziri.
rows.output: He also clearly targeted the Democrats in the House, accusing them of "outrageous conduct in the House, obstruction" by the radical Democrats and their anger at Hillary Clinton's defeat in the 2016 presidential election.
rows.reference: He also explicitly condemned Democrats on the committee, calling the allegations against him a "grotesque and coordinated character assassination" organized by liberals angry that Hillary Clinton lost the 2016 presidential election.

rows.source: Pelosi kwuru na ọ kwenyere na akaebe nke Kavanaugh gosiri ọ nweghị ike ịrụ ọrụ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị, n’ihi o gosiri na ọ nweghị mmasị n’ebe ndị Demokrat nọ.
rows.output: Pelosi said she believes the testimony of Kavanaugh shows that he cannot work in the Supreme Court, because it shows that he has no interest in the Democrats.
rows.reference: Pelosi said that she believed Kavanaugh's testimony proved that he could not serve on the Supreme Court, because it showed that he is biased against Democrats.

rows.source: O kwuru “echere m na ọ kagburu onwe ya site na iji okwu ndị ahụ yana n’ụzọ o si kwutọọ Clintons yana ndị Demokrat,”
rows.output: He said, "I thought he was discrediting himself by using those words and the way he was insulting the Clintons and the Democrats."
rows.reference: "I think that he disqualifies himself with those statements and the manner in which he went after the Clintons and the Democrats," she said.

rows.source: Pelosi dajụrụ mgbe ajụrụ ma ọ ga-achọ iwepu Kavanaugh ma ọ bụrụ na etinye ya n’oche, ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Demokrat nweta ọnụọgụgụ karịrị na Ụlọ nke Ndị Nnọchite.
rows.output: Pelosi hesitated when asked if she would seek to remove Kavanaugh if he were seated, if the Democrats were to gain a majority in the House of Representatives.
rows.reference: Pelosi demurred when asked if she would try to impeach Kavanaugh if he is confirmed, and if Democrats gain the majority in the House of Representatives.

rows.source: “M ga-ekwu nke a -- ọ bụrụ na ọ naghị agwa Kọngress ma ọ bụ ndị FBI eziokwu, mgbe ahụ ọ bụghị naanị na o tozughi ịnọ na Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị, ma ị nọ n’ụlọ ikpe ọ nọ na ya ugbu a,” Pelosi kwuru.
rows.output: "I'm going to say this -- if he's not telling the Congress or the FBI the truth, then he's not only not staying in the Supreme Court, you're in a court that you are now in."
rows.reference: "I will say this -- if he is not telling the truth to Congress or to the FBI, then he's not fit not only to be on the Supreme Court, but to be on the court he's on right now," Pelosi said.

rows.source: Kavanaugh bụ nnukwu ọka ikpe na D.C. Ụlọ Ikpe Sekuit nke Arịrịọ Mkpegharị.
rows.output: Kavanaugh is a senior judge on the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals.
rows.reference: Kavanaugh is currently a judge on the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals.

rows.source: Pelosi kwukwara na ka onye Demokrat na ọ nwere nchegbu maka ntimiwu Kavanaugh ga-adị maka Affordable Care Act ma ọ bụ Roe v. Wade, ebe a na ahụta ya ka akwụmụtọ na egbochi mgbanwe.

rows.output: From FWC, there are reports of a decline in the population of small coastal communities in Pinellas, Manatee, Sarasota, Charlotte, and Collier counties - which are attributed to a combination of factors and a reduction in population.
rows.reference: According to the FWC, patchier bloom conditions are being reported in areas of Pinellas, Manatee, Sarasota, Charlotte and Collier counties - which suggests decreasing concentrations.
